claims.text: A data-driven synthesis–simulation feedback loop can enable formation of noble-metal high-entropy alloys as three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
The feedback-loop method can provide greater atomic-level precision than conventional synthesis methods.
Conventionally synthesized NM-HEA precursors have disordered atomic arrangements.
Conventionally synthesized NM-HEA precursors lack a defined three-dimensional framework.
A machine-learning-integrated synthesis–simulation loop can continuously adjust temperature, deposition rate, and elemental composition during fabrication.
The proposed synthesis can be conducted from ambient to moderate temperatures with real-time process monitoring and feedback.
Feedback-mediated control of nucleation and growth can establish an interconnected, porous, three-dimensional nanoframework.
High-throughput synthesis data can be analyzed by a machine-learning model to predict conditions favorable for atomic ordering.
On-the-fly refinement of process parameters can steer nucleation and atomic assembly.
Steering nucleation and atomic assembly can produce a three-dimensional framework with precise atomic control.
The proposed method will produce NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks with high surface area.
The proposed method will produce NM-HEA nanoframeworks with well-controlled atomic arrangements.
The resulting nanoframeworks will have better catalytic properties than frameworks produced by conventional methods.
Conventional methods such as arc melting and magnetron sputtering yield either non-framework nanostructures or frameworks with less atomic-level precision.
The method may be unreliable outside the synthesis-parameter range represented in the training dataset.
The scalability of the method to industrial-scale production has not been validated.
The quantitative relationship between process-parameter adjustments and atomic ordering is uncertain.
TEM, XRD, and BET measurements can compare framework architecture, phase or ordering, and surface area between feedback-controlled and conventional syntheses.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field categorically says conventionally produced precursors lack a defined 3D framework, whereas the baseline allows conventional methods to produce frameworks, albeit with lower atomic-level precision.
